newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy economy still flat, rate cut can help -- ISCO.
newsitem.headline: Italy economy still flat, rate cut can help -- ISCO.

text.p: Italy's economy remains flat but the fall in inflation and a tight budget leaves space for a fall in interest rates that can help a recovery, state economic research group ISCO said in its monthly report.

"Towards the end of 1996, the Italian economy remains characterised by a sustained stagnation of productive acitivity," it said. But the internal picture shows nevertheless a substantial improvement that confirms the possibility of rivitalising the recovery, added the report.

ISCO said the stability of the exchange rate, the fall in inflation and improved public finances will leave a margin for reducing interest rates which should progressively lead to an improvement in the economy.
The report noted that real Italian interest rates, slightly higher than five percent, are higher than many of Italy's European partners.
